candidates.buyer: Licensed cashew intermediaries and buying-post operators, with the exporters who hire them (about 1,700 to 2,100 per season)
candidates.category: 31. Cashew intermediaries and buying posts (22. commodity traders)
candidates.evidence: Lusa/DN 2018 https://www.dn.pt/lusa/interior/governo-da-guine-bissau-baixa-preco-da-licenca-para-exportacao-do-caju-9238930.html (fetched); Forbes Africa Lusófona 2026 https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=169801; 2025 counts of 2,099 intermediary licences and 500 evacuation permits in the ANCA search results (Lusa, via https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=169899 and related)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Portuguese, 'software intermediários caju Guiné-Bissau rastreabilidade licenças ANCA') found none local. Only generic cashew traceability vendors (TraceX), not tied to ANCA or Guinea-Bissau.
candidates.known_note: K02 targets exporters and intermediaries as a pack. This one is specifically the licensed buying-post intermediaries, a larger and different buyer group, but the duty overlaps heavily.
candidates.name: Cashew buying-post intermediary licence, evacuation permit and campaign-compliance pack
candidates.trigger: Annual campaign (opens March): Ministry of Commerce intermediary licence and evacuation permit, fixed purchase price (478 CFA/kg in Bissau for 2026), bags stamped with origin and harvest year, DGVTT special circulation permit for trucks to Bissau, ANCA ordinance on operators' obligations.
candidates.unchecked: Whether ANCA or Commerce run an online licence portal; licence fee for intermediaries; whether intermediaries are digitally literate or pay; seasonality (about 6 months); current 2026 ordinance text.

candidates.buyer: Truck owners and hauliers moving cashew to Bissau
candidates.known_note: Same campaign but a different buyer (hauliers).
candidates.name: Cashew truck circulation-permit and evacuation tracking for hauliers
candidates.trigger: DGVTT issues the only special circulation authorisation for vehicles carrying cashew to Bissau (2018 rule); evacuation permits per consignment.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the permit still exists in 2026; volume of hauliers; any fee.

candidates.buyer: Small shops and traders with annual turnover of about 10-40M XOF who opt for or fall into the simplified VAT regime
candidates.evidence: https://kpmg.com/us/en/taxnewsflash/news/2025/02/guinea-bissau-vat-implementation-2025.html and https://www.vatupdate.com/2025/01/22/guinea-bissau-introduces-new-vat-regime-thresholds-and-simplified-option-for-taxpayers/ (search snippets, not fetched); Kontaktu DGCI https://kontaktu.mef.gw (DECIRF, DCI-SMT)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Portuguese, 'IVA pequenos contribuintes regime simplificado Kontaktu comerciantes') found no private tool or step-by-step guide; Kontaktu itself is free and hosts the filing.
candidates.known_note: K01 sells to accounting offices. This one sells to the small traders themselves; the duty (IVA returns) is the same.
candidates.name: IVA simplified-regime (5%) filing service for small traders
candidates.trigger: Law 4/2022, VAT live 1 Jan 2025 (Circular 20/GDGCI/2024); registration above 10M XOF; simplified regime at 5%; periodic returns on Kontaktu (monthly or quarterly, sources conflict).
candidates.unchecked: Actual count of simplified-regime taxpayers; official return frequency; whether Kontaktu usability is a pain; willingness to pay below 10M XOF turnover (exempt).

candidates.buyer: Pirogue owners and artisanal fishing operators, fish traders
candidates.name: Artisanal fishing vessel licence, sanitary licence and landing compliance
candidates.trigger: Decree 24/2011 Artisanal Fishing Regulation; 2016 joint orders: navigation licence (Instituto Marítimo Portuário), sanitary licence, landing in national territory; 2% or 5% stamp duty on fishing licences with a 500,000 FCFA floor (industrial/company scale).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the 2016 orders are in force and enforced; number of licensed pirogues; any current registry or fee.

candidates.buyer: Fish processors and traders exporting regionally
candidates.name: Fish processors and exporters: pescado inspection and EU-access compliance
candidates.trigger: 2011 Regulamento de Inspecção de Pescado; EU import ban pending CIPA lab accreditation.
candidates.unchecked: Number of firms; whether EU access is still blocked; current inspection fees and reporting.

candidates.existing: Antares Vision is the state's supplier, likely a free-to-user government system. No local competitor search run (budget at cap).
candidates.name: Pharmacy and medicine-importer track-and-trace compliance (national mandate)
candidates.trigger: Sept 2025 Ministry of Health Track and Trace mandate and National Medicines Catalogue with Antares Vision.
candidates.unchecked: Whether pharmacies must scan or report; deadlines; number of licensed pharmacies; whether the state system already gives them a free interface.

candidates.buyer: Orange Money and Telecel Money agents (sole traders)
candidates.evidence: LinkedIn analysis of Guinea-Bissau financial inclusion (search snippet), https://sn.linkedin.com/in/olivier-yao; no agent licensing rule found
candidates.name: Mobile money agent (Orange Money, Telecel) compliance and float reporting
candidates.trigger: BCEAO EME and agent framework (regional); operator KYC rules.
candidates.unchecked: Whether any authority-facing duty falls on agents; operators likely supply their own apps.

candidates.name: Timber trader export licence and CITES documentation
candidates.trigger: Export moratorium from 2015; 2021 plan to lift it with 14 species under quotas (promulgation unconfirmed); CITES Pterocarpus erinaceus rules.
candidates.unchecked: Current ban status; licensing regime; associated corruption makes a paid tool unlikely.

candidates.buyer: Sand, gravel and clay quarry operators
candidates.name: Small-scale sand, gravel and quarry operator licence compliance
candidates.trigger: Law 3/2014 Mining and Quarrying Code; Decree 33/87 on quarries.
candidates.unchecked: Licence procedure, fees and reporting for small operators; count of operators.

candidates.buyer: Bissau market traders and bideiras; Câmara Municipal de Bissau
candidates.name: Informal trader and municipal market-fee formalisation
candidates.trigger: Nov 2023 formalisation incentive programme (terms unpublished); daily municipal fee about 150 CFA.
candidates.unchecked: Any formal registration scheme; very low willingness to pay.

candidates.name: NGO and association annual reporting
candidates.trigger: Decree-Law 23/92; no annual reporting duty confirmed.
candidates.unchecked: Any 2024-2026 amendment; reporting to the Ministry of Justice.

candidates.buyer: Manual-exchange bureaux, SFDs and savings groups
candidates.name: Bureaux de change and SFD (microfinance) regulatory reporting
candidates.trigger: BCEAO regulation on manual exchange and SFD supervision (regional, UMOA).
candidates.unchecked: Number of live institutions; monthly reports and which BCEAO systems they use; Guinea-Bissau specifics.

candidates.known_note: Same buyer and duty; the 2024 labour code is context only.
candidates.name: Domestic-worker INSS registration and payslip service
candidates.trigger: INSS; new labour code regulates domestic service (2024).

candidates.known_note: Kontaktu hosts DECIRF; consistent with K06 rejection.
candidates.name: Payroll and contribution filing

candidates.known_note: No new evidence to revive K05.
candidates.name: Standalone e-invoicing / invoice compliance
Cashew exporter campaign pack (about 20 export licences in 2025, mostly Indian firms)
candidates.trigger: Annual export licence from Ministry of Commerce; ANCA ordinance

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03. A 2024 article (Univ. Lisbon repository) says the new labour code regulates the domestic service contract for the first time; ISCTE 2021 thesis on extending social security to domestic work in Bissau; association ANAPROMED. No official INSS registration procedure found. Employer INSS 14% / employee 8% only from payroll-vendor sites (unverified).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget spent on higher-yield categories. No sources surfaced incidentally.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; nothing surfaced incidentally.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; nothing surfaced incidentally.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Cattle and pasteurised milk are imported from Senegal; exports to Senegal are informal (Lusa, May 2025). Veterinary body is the DGE (livestock directorate) per WOAH PVS reports. No livestock trader licensing or movement-permit rule found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Nothing found on abattoir or butcher licensing in the livestock search. Unverified.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: WOAH PVS evaluations (2008, follow-up 2015, gap analysis 2019) show weak veterinary services and a shortage of animal-health auxiliaries. No private vet registration or reporting duty found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: No 2024-2025 NGO or association reporting law found. Core statute is Decree-Law 23/92 (EU civil society roadmap 2021-2025); recognition goes through notaries. No annual reporting duty confirmed.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: A federation groups 21 driver and owner associations (taxi, toca-toca, candonga). No licensing, vehicle registration or motor insurance rule found for Guinea-Bissau. Cashew trucks need a DGVTT special circulation permit (see candidate).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Bissau street vendors (bideiras) pay about 150 CFA a day to the Câmara Municipal (RTP). The PM announced an informal-sector formalisation programme in Nov 2023 with no terms published. Money changers: BCEAO manual-exchange framework is regional; no Guinea-Bissau specifics found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: No driving-school or technical-inspection rule found. The national driving licence exists (PRADO, first issued 2012); the road code replaced the Portuguese 1954 code. Nothing else found.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Fuel mostly imported from Senegal and Portugal; Petromar (Galp-linked) supplier; importers press for price updates (Forbes Africa Lusófona, undated). Decree 1/77 created Guiné-Gás with an import and distribution monopoly (FAOLEX, status unverified). No station licence or reporting rule found.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Cashew is the dominant commodity. See candidates 31a-31c. Export licence (alvará), intermediary licences, bag labelling, circulation permits. No digital ANCA licensing platform found.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: BCEAO monograph (2010) counted 18 SFDs, only 5 operating. Regional UMOA SFD rules apply. No current cotisation or reporting data found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: No dedicated search. Health insurance is minimal in the country; no sources surfaced.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: No pharmacy licensing rule found. Sept 2025: Ministry of Health signed a national Track and Trace mandate for medicines with Antares Vision, centred on a National Medicines Catalogue. Pharmacy and importer obligations under it are unverified.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; budget.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining and Quarrying Code is Law 3/2014; quarries under Decree 33/87. Small-scale activity is mostly sand, gravel, clay, granite. No small-operator licence procedure found; bauxite (Boé) and phosphate are large-firm.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: OHADA computerised RCCM deployed in Guinea-Bissau (ohada.com). Regional UEMOA/GIABA AML rules apply. No specific periodic report for notaries or brokers found.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: No Guinea-Bissau guest-register or tourism-levy rule found; results were Portugal-only. Unverified.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Fish: Regulamento de Inspecção de Pescado (2011); EU export ban not lifted per European Parliament text, CIPA lab accreditation pending. Timber: export moratorium since 2015, a 2021 lifting plan with 14 species and quotas (promulgation unconfirmed), CITES pau-sangue rules. Cashew: see 31 series.

coverage.category: 31. Cashew intermediaries and buying posts (country-specific)
coverage.found: 2,099 intermediary licences and 500 evacuation permits issued by mid-campaign 2025; over 1,700 post intermediaries in 2024; fixed Bissau buying price 478 CFA/kg in 2026; bag stamp with origin and harvest year; DGVTT circulation permit. See candidates.

coverage.category: 32. Artisanal fishing vessels and fish exporters (country-specific)
coverage.found: Artisanal Fishing Regulation, Decree 24/2011; 2016 joint orders require navigation licence from the Instituto Marítimo Portuário, a sanitary licence, and landing in national territory; implementation described as weak. No 2025 registry found.

coverage.category: 33. Mobile money agents (Orange Money, Telecel Money) (country-specific)
coverage.found: Orange Money and Telecel Money are the two main EMEs; Orange agent network is dominant. No agent licensing or reporting rule specific to Guinea-Bissau found.

coverage.category: 34. IVA (VAT) since 1 Jan 2025: small taxpayers and simplified regime (country-specific)
coverage.found: Law 4/2022, Circular 20/GDGCI/2024. Registration above 10M XOF in 12 months; simplified option for 10-40M XOF at a 5% rate (secondary sources, conflicting on monthly or quarterly returns). Kontaktu hosts DECIRF and DCI-SMT filings.

coverage.category: 35. Informal-trader formalisation and municipal market fees (country-specific)
coverage.found: Nov 2023 government announcement of a formalisation incentive programme, no terms published. Municipal collections often not reaching the treasury. No tariff table found.

coverage.category: 36. Medicines track-and-trace mandate (country-specific, 2025)
coverage.found: Antares Vision mandate signed Sept 2025 for pharmaceutical traceability; scope for pharmacies unverified.
